title: Pharmacokinetics of antenatal steroidprophylaxis with betamethasone phosphate after intravenous administration
summary:
If a child is likely to be born significantly premature, pregnant women are given the drug betamethasone monophosphate. This drug supports the maturation of the unborn child's lungs. Until now, it has usually been administered as an injection into a muscle. However, there has not yet been sufficient research into how well the drug works when administered directly into a vein.
In this study, we want to find out whether the drug reaches the mother's blood in sufficient quantities when administered intravenously. It is important that the amount of the active ingredient in the blood remains high enough over a certain period of time.
Twelve pregnant women who are at increased risk of premature birth are participating in the study. The decision to treat is made independently of the study according to medical standards.
All participants will receive the drug intravenously in the hospital over a period of 48 hours. During this time, a total of fifteen small blood samples will be taken at specified times. This will allow us to measure how the amount of the active ingredient in the blood changes over time.
The pregnancy will continue to be monitored until birth. The aim of the study is to create a better basis for the use of this form of treatment.

interventions.name:
- Steroid prophylaxis with 2 x 3 ampoules of Celestan solubile intravenously over 48 hours
(Composition of one ampoule of Celestan solubile: 4.0 mg betamethasone dihydrogen phosphate)
- 15 serial plasma level checks of betamethasone at the following times: 0.25 hours, 0.5 hours, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Intact singleton pregnancy
- Gestational age between 23+0 and 33+6 weeks at study inclusion
- Threatened preterm birth with indication for antenatal steroid prophylaxis in accordance with current medical standards
Exclusion criteria:
- Multiple pregnancies
- Triple I (amniotic infection syndrome)
- Therapy with systemically active corticosteroids within the last seven days prior to study inclusion and during the measurement periods
- Incapacity to give consent
- Impaired liver function (ASAT/ALAT > 2x the upper normal value)
- Anemia with hemoglobin concentration < 6.0 mmol/L
- Cardiac valve defects ≥ II°, signs of cardiac insufficiency (≥ NYHA III)
Study protocol BetaIV, version 2.1
- Birth within 48 hours after the start of antenatal steroid prophylaxis
